## Summary

Built `/strongarm.icl` — a mirror-symmetric StrongARM latch comparator at SKY130 level-2 assembly. Key design decisions:

- **Symmetry axis**: `M0.cx` (tail transistor centered at origin), used consistently for every `pair` statement (M1/M2, M3/M4, M5/M6, M7/M8, M9/M10).
- **Vertical stacking**: All pairs stacked with `above=... gap=min` — tail at bottom, input pair, cross-coupled NMOS, then three PMOS rows. This keeps everything compact and mirror-symmetric about one vertical axis.
- **Taps**: `ptap` (VGND) below M0 for the NMOS substrate; `ntap` (VPWR) below the top PMOS row for the n-well islands.
- **Guard ring**: `ntap` ring around all six PMOS devices (M5–M10) to enclose their shared n-well.
- **Routing**: All nets routed with appropriate widths; symmetric nets (CLK, INP/INN, OUTP/OUTN, P/Q) rely on the mirrored placement for symmetry.

The hardest part was getting the `pair` syntax right — it only accepts `above`/`below`/`at_y`/`axis`/`gap`/`vgap`, not `left_of`/`right_of`, so all placement had to be expressed as vertical stacking rather than horizontal abutment.
